verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean never writes the normalizing power q^{A+1/2}: it keeps the unnormalized physical chart and carries q inside `carrier`. The rewriting is the paper's own normalization. `carrier` is `heatAmplitude = C · s^{-A} 𝓗(2τ/s)` with s = r²/2 = qX and 2τ/s = 2d/X, i.e. carrier = q^{-A} E_pow(X) 𝓗(2d/X) with E_pow = C X^{-A} (`spatialExponent (1+h) = 1/2 - (1+h) = -A`); and `radius² = 2 q X`, so radius = √q·√(2X). Hence q^{A+1/2}·carrier·(2/radius) = 2 E_pow(X)𝓗(2d/X)/√(2X). Combining `radialTaper_deriv` (f_r = (2/r) f', with f' = (edge 4 δ/δ³)·taperSlopeFactor by `tailShapeDeriv_factorization`) with `boundaryCoefficient` gives K f_r = (edge 4 δ/δ³)·boundaryCoefficient, which is the display after multiplication by q^{A+1/2}. The profile-chart variant `profileBoundaryCoefficient` is literally 2·E_pow(X)𝓗(2d/X)/√(2X) · taperSlopeFactor, because q is normalized to 1 there. No constant, exponent or sign differs.
